scenes.name: Nu disco
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: El regreso nostálgico del gran tesoro de la música disco en todas sus etapas, de las producciones orquestales a las variaciones electrónicas; su límite es el nacimiento del house.

podcast.title: Breakthrough at 35
podcast.body: James Murphy, already 35 and showing signs of aging, achieved his breakthrough with LCD Sound System's self-titled debut album in 2005, following years of working in the indie scene and with his label. "But at the time all this happened, James Murphy was 35 and going gray."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Co-founded DFA Records
podcast.body: About a year after declining the *Seinfeld* offer, James Murphy co-founded the indie label DFA, an acronym for Death From Above, working with New York City indie artists for eight years. "About a year later, he started up an indie label called DFA, which stood for Death From Above."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Declined Seinfeld Scriptwriting Job
podcast.body: James Murphy was once offered a job as a scriptwriter for the popular TV show *Seinfeld*. He turned down this opportunity to instead continue pursuing his music career, which ultimately led to the formation of LCD Soundsystem. "James Murphy was once offered a job as a script writer for Seinfeld, but he turned that down in favor of sticking with music, which resulted in LCD sound system."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

podcast.title: Declined Seinfeld Writing Offer (Age 22)
podcast.body: As an English major dropout, James Murphy was offered a writing position for a new TV show called *Seinfeld* at age 22, but he declined, believing the show "about nothing" would not work, choosing instead to focus on music. "But then he thought, eh, this show is never going to work. It's about nothing. Pass. I'll stick with my music instead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Regret Over Black Star Production
podcast.body: James Murphy, unaware of David Bowie's terminal illness at the time of Black Star's recording, later expressed profound regret for not fully committing to the album's production. He has stated in interviews that it was the "biggest mistake of his life" not to have paid more attention to David Bowie's request. "es algo que hoy en día en sus entrevistas dice que se revendirá toda su vida, dice que había sido el mayor error de su vida no haber hecho más caso a David Bowie."

podcast.title: Rejected Producer Role for Black Star
podcast.body: James Murphy was initially slated to be a co-producer for David Bowie's Black Star alongside Bowie and Tony Visconti. However, due to his intense involvement in numerous other projects—including his own record label, collaborations, productions, and event organization—he was unable to dedicate sufficient time, often being late or absent from sessions and struggling to understand Bowie's experimental material. He ultimately declined full producer credit, contributing only specific rhythmic and sound elements. "Finalmente, James Murphy terminó rechazando el trabajo como productor colaborador para el Black Star, él sí que trabajo en el álbum, haciendo algunas bases de sonidos de ritmos, poniendo algunas ideas, ayudando a producir alguna cosa pero su trabajo no dejo de ser un montón de cosas puntuales que se entremezclan en el disco."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
